t: Clovis is the earliest widely recognised archaeological culture of North America, found from southern Canada to northern Mexico around 13,050 to 12,750 years ago.
Its makers were highly mobile hunter-gatherers who carried fine stone tools hundreds of kilometres, relied on big game such as mammoths and bison, and also ate small animals and plants.

Older sites such as Monte Verde II in Chile show that Clovis people were not the first inhabitants of the Americas, and most researchers have abandoned the “Clovis First” model since the beginning of the 21st century.
dyk: Isotope analysis of Anzick-1, a young boy buried in Montana with over 100 stone and bone artefacts stained with red ochre, suggests that mammoth made up about 35–40 per cent of his group’s diet.
ev: Clovis points and tools come into use across North America, about 13,050 years ago by the dating of a 2020 study
A young boy, Anzick-1, is buried about 12,990 to 12,840 years ago in Montana with over 100 stone and bone artefacts stained with red ochre
About 12,750 to 12,600 years ago Clovis gives way to regional traditions, among them the Folsom tradition of central North America
Ridgely Whiteman, aged 19, discovers the Clovis site at Blackwater Draw in eastern New Mexico
Crews under Edgar Billings Howard and later John L. Cotter excavate the best-documented Clovis finds near Clovis, New Mexico
Paul S. Martin proposes the overkill hypothesis, that human hunters, Clovis peoples among them, drove the North American megafauna to extinction
The Anzick-1 burial is found near Wilsall, Montana

f.homeland: Across North America, from southern Canada to northern Mexico and across the east and west of the continent; the type site Blackwater Draw locality No. 1 near Clovis, New Mexico, with the Dent site in Colorado, the Gault site in Texas, Jake Bluff in Oklahoma, La Prele in Wyoming and the Anzick burial in Montana.
f.period: About 13,050 to 12,750 calibrated years Before Present, by a 2020 study of ten securely dated sites (some argue for sites as old as 13,500 years BP, others for a long chronology of about 1,500 years); succeeded from about 12,750–12,600 years BP by regional traditions such as Folsom.
f.known: fluted, lanceolate Clovis points; blades, bifaces and bevelled rods of bone, antler and ivory; caches of tools, over twenty known; hunting mammoths and other big game; red ochre and engraved stones; the Anzick-1 burial; the abandonment of the “Clovis First” model
f.sources: Excavation since the find at Blackwater Draw in 1929, by crews under Edgar Billings Howard and John L. Cotter from 1932 to 1937, and at many sites since; radiocarbon dating; studies of stone-tool making and wear; animal bones and isotope analysis; the genome of Anzick-1.
